codes.justification: The clause provides for adjustment of the Contract Price due to changes in taxes and duties, an adjustment mechanism analogous to price change provisions.

The clause allocates indemnification responsibility between the Owner and Design-Builder for claims arising from errors, omissions, negligence, or breach of contract, establishing a risk allocation mechanism between the parties.

The clause allocates responsibility and remedy for delays caused by court or public authority orders not due to the Construction Manager's fault, granting a termination right as risk allocation mechanism.

The clause expressly deals with disputes and matters in question between the Trade Contractor and Other Trade Contractors, referencing the Dispute Resolution provisions in Part 8 and arbitration consent mechanisms.

The clause defines disputes between the parties and requires that unresolved disputes be settled in accordance with the Dispute Resolution provisions of Part 8, establishing the trigger and process for formal dispute resolution.

The clause allocates the Owner's right to suspend or terminate the Contract if unwilling or unable to proceed, and defines the Construction Manager's responsibility upon such notice, allocating risk of project discontinuation.

The clause lists default triggers tied to failure to demonstrate financial arrangements, failure to certify or pay progress payments, and non-payment of certified/awarded amounts, all payment mechanics.
The clause allocates the risk of Owner default and establishes the Design-Builder's right to respond, forming part of contractual risk allocation for non-performance by the Owner.
Clause defines the cost basis for pricing work performed under a Change Directive, directly governing adjustment of costs attributable to changes in the Work.
Details the specific cost items and rates (labour, products, equipment, subcontract) that determine payment/compensation for work performed under a Change Directive.
References insurance premiums and losses subject to insurance policies (GC 11.1) as recoverable costs under the Change Directive.
The clause governs the process for claims that adjust the Contract Price, requiring notice of intent to claim, which is part of the change/claims mechanism under Part 6 Changes in the Work.
The clause requires establishing a date for finishing remaining Work following acceptance with reservation, addressing timing/scheduling of remaining work.

The clause establishes a broad contractor obligation to provide and pay for labour, Products, equipment, and services necessary for performing the Work in accordance with the Contract, a general execution duty.
The clause deems occupied portions of the Work to be taken over by the Owner, transferring responsibility and effectively passing control/title-like status from the Construction Manager to the Owner.
The clause reallocates responsibility for care and custody of the occupied part of the Work from the Construction Manager to the Owner upon early occupancy.
The clause addresses coordination between Shop Drawings and the Contract Documents, requiring identification and review of deviations to ensure design consistency.

The requirement for disclosure and Consultant acceptance/rejection of deviations functions as a quality assurance check confirming compliance with Contract Documents prior to fabrication/incorporation.
The clause directly addresses adjustment of insurance requirements under CCDC 41 upon a revised version reducing coverage requirements.
Any agreed reduction in insurance requirements must be recorded via a Change Order, tying the clause to the formal change mechanism.

The clause directly requires the Contractor to promptly correct defective work rejected by the Consultant for failing to conform to the Contract Documents, addressing correction of non-conforming Work.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Contractor for defects arising from poor workmanship, defective products, or carelessness, regardless of incorporation into the Work.
The clause requires Shop Drawings to be provided to the Consultant for review, ensuring coordination between the Contractor's submittals and the Contract Documents.
The clause requires Shop Drawings to be submitted per an agreed schedule or in orderly sequence, sufficiently in advance to avoid delay to the Work, tying submittal timing to sequencing of work.

This clause governs procedures for submitting and updating claims (interim and final accounts) under the waiver of claims provisions, forming part of the matters-in-question/claim process between the parties.
The clause addresses covering work designated for special tests, inspections or approvals, and requires uncovering to complete such inspections or tests.

The clause requires the Construction Manager to uncover work, complete inspections, and make good the covering work at its own expense, addressing correction/consequences for failing to allow inspection.
The clause establishes payment obligations owed to the Construction Manager upon termination, including timing of payment applications and reimbursable expenses.
The clause allocates responsibility for damages and losses sustained by the Construction Manager as a result of termination, addressing risk allocation upon contract termination.
The clause addresses disagreement over an expert's finding being settled through a dispute resolution process, indicating a formal mechanism for resolving matters in question between the parties.
The clause falls under GC 9.5 MOULD, addressing an environmental/hazard issue related to mould at the Place of the Work.

The clause governs the process for arbitration following mediation, including notice requirements and the jurisdiction where arbitration is conducted, as part of the dispute resolution mechanism under CCDC 40.

This clause establishes procedural requirements (notice within 10 Working Days) for claiming an extension of Contract Time due to delay, which is part of the change/adjustment provisions under Part 6 Changes in the Contract.
The clause governs the timing and submission process for monthly applications for payment on account, a core payment provision.

The clause conditions the addition of an Added Value Incentive Item on comparisons between Estimated Final Target Cost, Base Target Cost, and Final Target Cost, directly administering the Target Cost mechanism.

The clause ties eligibility for adding items to the Base Program to whether the Final Target Cost has been set, reflecting a baseline lock-in condition before which changes to the target cost figures remain adjustable.

This clause establishes a negotiation procedure requiring the parties to make reasonable efforts to resolve disputes amicably and disclose relevant information, forming part of the dispute resolution process under GC 8.3.
The clause addresses the Owner's failure to make payment as due under the Contract as a trigger for default notice.
The clause establishes a process for allocating and managing the risk of Owner default, including notice and cure period, protecting the Design/Construction Team's rights and remedies.

The clause requires the Owner to notify the Construction Manager upon observing a fault, defect, or non-conformity with the Contract, directly engaging the identification of defective or non-conforming Work.
The clause provides for adjustment of Contract Time and reimbursement of costs due to Owner-caused delay, which is a form of claim/adjustment under the contract's change provisions.
The clause allocates responsibility for delay caused by the Owner's action or omission, assigning risk of resulting time and cost impacts to the Owner.

The clause addresses disputes arising under the Contract and directs application of negotiation, mediation, and arbitration procedures as well as retention of rights provisions, establishing a dispute resolution process.

The clause establishes that the Contract, once agreed, may only be amended in accordance with the Contract Documents, effectively locking in the baseline agreement and requiring formal change provisions for modifications.
The clause references the mechanism by which the Contract may be amended, tying into the formal change provisions (Change Orders/Directives) governing adjustments to the Work or Contract Price.

The clause requires the Contract Price to be adjusted by Change Order to reconcile actual expenditures under the contingency allowance with the allowance amount, directly invoking the formal change mechanism.
The clause requires the Contractor to maintain cost accounts and records specifically related to a Change Directive, supporting the administration of changes to the Work and Contract Price.

This clause addresses the scope and limits of a Change Directive, a formal mechanism for adjusting the Work, Contract Price, or Contract Time, by clarifying it cannot be used solely to change Contract Time.
The clause provides for adjustment of Contract Price and Contract Time due to suspension, referencing the delay adjustment provisions, which is a change-adjustment mechanism.
The clause requires the PMT to establish a date for finishing the Work following Ready-for-Takeover, addressing the completion/performance of the Work under the Contract Documents.
Establishing a date for finishing the Work relates to timing/sequencing following Ready-for-Takeover, a scheduling milestone.
The clause conditions Owner occupancy on approval by authorities having jurisdiction, managing compliance risk associated with early occupancy of the Work.
This clause addresses authorization of expenditures under cash allowances, which relates to payment application and approval mechanics through the Consultant.
The clause addresses exposure to toxic or hazardous substances and property damage/destruction from such substances at the Place of the Work, an express environmental/hazardous substance obligation.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner to take reasonable steps regarding pre-existing hazardous substances, an allocation of risk between the parties.

The clause establishes a formal notice-of-dispute and reply procedure, including deemed waiver if a party fails to dispute a finding within specified time limits, which is a core dispute resolution mechanism.

The clause addresses the Design-Builder's continuing responsibility for errors or omissions in the Construction Documents and compliance with the Contract Documents, a design coordination/consistency matter.
The clause allocates responsibility for errors/omissions and non-conformity to the Design-Builder despite Owner's review, unless a written deviation is accepted, which is a risk allocation provision.
The clause implies that deviations from the accepted Contract Documents require formal written acceptance by the Owner, reflecting a locked baseline requiring formal change to modify.
The clause requires preparation, monitoring, and updating of the Construction Schedule, addressing timing, critical events, and interrelationships of Work activities.
The clause establishes a duty on the Construction Manager to organize and monitor performance of the Work in conformity with the Contract Time.
The clause references revisions to the Construction Schedule resulting from extensions of Contract Time under the Changes provisions of the General Conditions.

The clause addresses responsibility for design errors/omissions in Owner-provided designs and Specifications, and the Design-Builder's review and acceptance process, which is a design coordination/responsibility issue.
The clause allocates risk between Owner and Design-Builder for design errors and omissions, shifting responsibility only upon written acceptance by the Design-Builder.

Clause allocates control/responsibility to the Owner to object to and require substitution of a proposed Trade Subcontractor or Supplier for reasonable cause, managing risk associated with subcontractor selection.

Establishes required insurance coverages (automobile, aircraft/watercraft, contractors' equipment, commercial general liability) to be provided and maintained by the Consultant, Contractor and Other IPD Parties, with durations specified per CCDC 41 requirements.

The clause allocates responsibility for obtaining and maintaining insurance among multiple parties and their subconsultants/subcontractors, functioning as a mechanism to manage contractual risk exposure.

This clause establishes procedural requirements for submitting a claim following a Notice in Writing under the waiver of claims provisions, forming part of the process for handling matters in question between the parties.

The clause governs how Change Directives are structured for valuing changes in the Work, requiring unrelated changes not be grouped together, which is a procedural requirement for administering changes to the Work.
The clause addresses the Owner's financial arrangements to fulfill payment obligations under the Contract, requiring notice of material changes affecting the Owner's ability to pay.
This clause addresses the Consultant's finding process for claims for a change in Contract Price, part of the change/claims mechanism under Part 6 Changes.

The Consultant's issuance of a finding by Notice in Writing on a claim is a step in resolving matters in question between the parties, establishing a procedural mechanism for addressing disputed claims.
The clause references options in paragraphs 7.2 and 7.3, which correspond to GMP and Target Contract Price provisions, establishing when these mechanisms may be agreed to.
The clause specifies that any agreement to exercise the options after signing shall be recorded via a Change Order, tying the option adoption to the formal change mechanism.
The clause describes the Consultant's role in evaluating payment applications and issuing certificates for payment under Article A-5 and GC 5.3, directly addressing payment certification.

The clause amends the contract upon exercise of the Stipulated Price option, tying the Contract Price definition (including taxes/duties) to the pricing mechanism established via Change Order under Article A-10 options.
The clause addresses what is included in the Contract Price and payment of Value Added Taxes by the Owner to the Construction Manager.
The clause addresses final payment application rejection/revision and compliance with Payment Legislation, part of the payment certification process.

The clause establishes that copyright and property ownership of design documents, drawings, and specifications remains with the Consultant/Other Consultants, regardless of payment or execution of the Work, and prohibits alteration by the Owner.

This clause establishes the procedure for submitting a claim for a change in Contract Price, requiring a detailed account and grounds, with the Consultant making a finding, directly implementing the claims mechanism under GC 6.6.

Establishes obligations for coordinating the activities and work of Other Trade Contractors, the Owner's and Construction Manager's own forces with the Work of the Contract, a broader work-execution coordination duty.
Requires that insurance coverage for Other Trade Contractors be provided consistent with GC 11.1 and coordinated with the Trade Contractor's insurance.
This clause imposes a general obligation on the Contractor to perform and fulfill all requirements of the Contract Documents, which is a core Work Execution duty.

The clause requires the Contractor to notify the Consultant and arrange inspections by authorities when work is designated for tests, inspections or approvals, establishing inspection procedures and notification duties.
The clause is part of GC 5.6 Progressive Release of Holdback, addressing obligations tied to certificates issued in connection with holdback release for subcontract work or Products.
The clause makes the Design-Builder responsible for correction of defects or work not performed, regardless of whether apparent at time of certificate issuance.
The clause allocates ongoing responsibility to the Design-Builder for protection and correction of work despite issuance of certificates, effectively assigning risk notwithstanding certification.

The clause requires the Contractor to correct or pay for damage resulting from corrections made under warranty obligations, directly addressing correction of defective/non-conforming Work and consequences thereof.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Contractor for damage arising from warranty corrections, an allocation of risk/responsibility.
The clause provides for adjustment of the Contract Price and Contract Time when the Owner requires a change of Subcontractor or Supplier, which is a form of price/time adjustment mechanism.

The clause defines the scope of labour, Products, and services required for performance of the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents, establishing the general execution obligation of the Contractor.

The clause preserves the Trade Contractor's obligations for quality, correction, and warranty of work performed prior to termination, directly addressing correction of non-conforming or defective work.
The clause allocates continuing responsibility to the Trade Contractor for conformity of its work even after termination, an allocation of contractual risk.
The clause addresses testing and inspection costs and responsibility for tests/inspections required by the Contract Documents or applicable laws, directly relating to inspection procedures.
The clause allocates who bears the cost of tests and inspections, which is a payment/cost-responsibility provision.
The clause describes the Payment Certifier's determination of amounts owing and issuance of certificates for progress and final payment, directly addressing payment certification mechanics.
The clause requires that any change in the Work be authorized through a Change Order or Change Directive, directly governing the formal change mechanism under the Contract.

This clause directly implements the Change Directive mechanism, requiring the Trade Contractor to proceed with a change in the Work upon receipt, which is a core part of the change process governed by Part 6.
The clause imposes an execution obligation on the Trade Contractor to promptly perform the changed Work.
The clause governs the timing and release of holdback amounts to the Contractor, subject to Payment Legislation and lien legislation, which is a core payment mechanic.
The clause requires that all required insurance policies be with insurers licensed in the jurisdiction of the Place of the Work, directly addressing insurance requirements applicable to the Contract.
The clause imposes a duty on the Contractor to determine the location of underground utilities before commencing work, establishing a requirement governing how the Work is to be performed.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Contractor for identifying underground utilities and structures, managing risk of damage to hidden site conditions before work begins.
The clause requires the Contractor to obtain inspections and certificates necessary for performance of the Work, a form of inspection obligation required by authorities having jurisdiction.
The clause establishes a contractor duty regarding procurement of permits and certifications necessary for performing the Work, part of executing the Work in compliance with regulatory requirements.
The clause establishes the amount of Value Added Taxes payable by the Owner to the Design-Builder, which is part of the payment provisions of the Contract Price.
Establishes payment obligations to Design/Construction Team members, including holdback, Payment Legislation compliance, and payment timing tied to Substantial Performance and Warranty Phase.
Payments are tied to Reimbursable Costs and Profit Pool, which are components of the target cost arrangement administered under the Contract.
The clause administers and adjusts the Profit Pool based on comparison of the Final Target Cost against the Base Target Cost, directly relating to the target cost mechanism.
Clause establishes the mediation process, including appointment of a Project Mediator and reference to CCDC 40 rules, as part of the dispute resolution procedure.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Trade Contractor for damage caused during performance of the Contract, assigning liability and cost for making good such damage.
The clause requires establishing a completion date for remaining Work following Substantial Performance, addressing scheduling of the remaining work.

The clause expressly declares that discovered artifacts, fossils, and items of value found at the Place of the Project are the absolute property of the Owner, establishing ownership/title of such items as between the parties.
The clause governs the effectiveness and recording of agreed adjustments to Contract Price and Contract Time in a Change Order, a core changes-in-the-work mechanism.
The clause requires that the value of work performed under a Change Order be included in progress payment applications, directly addressing payment mechanics.
The clause addresses when payments become due to the Design-Builder in relation to insurance loss events, directly governing payment mechanics.
The clause explicitly references property and boiler and machinery insurance policies and payment following loss or damage, tying payment to insurance coverage under GC 11.1.

The clause requires Shop Drawings to be submitted according to an agreed schedule or in orderly sequence sufficiently in advance to avoid causing delay, directly addressing sequencing and timing of submissions relative to the Work.
Shop Drawings review by the Consultant is part of coordinating design details with the performance of the Work to ensure compatibility with Contract Documents.
Requires submission of a schedule of values before the first application for payment for the Work and periodic updates, directly governing payment application procedures.
Establishes the warranty period during which defective or non-conforming Work must be corrected under the Contract, tying the warranty term to the Ready for Acceptance With Reservation milestone.
The clause directs that changes in cost or time caused by discovered artifacts/fossils be addressed through Change Order or Change Directive procedures, adjusting the Contract Price/Time.

The clause allocates responsibility for handling unforeseen site conditions (artifacts/fossils) by requiring investigation and appropriate contractual response, reflecting risk management for such discoveries.
The clause addresses what the Contract Price includes and the treatment of Value Added Taxes payable by the Owner, which relates to payment mechanics under the contract.

The clause governs the process for reviewing and deciding upon requests for a Contract Amendment, which is the mechanism for adjusting the Work and Contract terms, requiring SMT approval for specific changes.

By requiring SMT approval for changes to the Agreement, Definitions and General Conditions, the clause reinforces that the accepted contractual baseline can only be altered through formal change/amendment procedures.
The clause treats Construction Documents as a fixed baseline that can only be altered through formal change mechanisms, reflecting a design lock-in principle.
The clause expressly directs that changes to the Construction Documents must proceed through GC 6.1, 6.2, or 6.3 governing Owner's right to change, Change Orders, and Change Directives.
Establishes requirements for progress payment applications including receipted vouchers and statutory declarations regarding payment of accounts and holdback amounts.

The clause describes the Consultant's role in evaluating payment applications and issuing certificates for payment under the Agreement and payment-related GCs, directly addressing payment certification.

This clause allocates risk between the parties by waiving and releasing certain claims while carving out exceptions, effectively managing and limiting liability exposure between the Owner and Trade Contractor.
The exceptions explicitly preserve claims for 'substantial defects or deficiencies in the Work' and warranty claims under GC 12.3, tying the waiver framework to defective work concepts.
The clause allocates a contractual remedy allowing the Contractor to suspend or terminate the Contract following unresolved default, managing risk of Owner non-performance.

The clause requires parties to engage a Project Mediator to attempt resolution of unresolved disputes following the reply period, applying CCDC 40 mediation rules, which is a formal dispute-resolution mechanism.

This clause governs the submission of claims accounts (interim and final) arising from a claim under the Waiver of Claims provisions, part of the procedural mechanism for asserting and resolving claims between the parties.

The clause establishes how the amount claimed in an application for payment is calculated, based on the value of Work performed and Products delivered as of the payment period end, which is a payment mechanics provision.
Clause governs the timing and consolidation of arbitration proceedings under the negotiation, mediation and arbitration article, directly establishing dispute resolution procedure.

The clause directs that changes required due to legal variances or subsequent law changes be issued through Change Order, Change Directive, or Owner's right to make changes provisions, tying required modifications to the formal change mechanism.

The clause allocates responsibility, relieving the Trade Contractor of the duty to verify legal compliance of the Contract Documents while placing the onus on notification and Owner-directed correction.
The clause addresses payment of portions of the Profit Pool at defined milestones, which is a payment mechanism under the Contract.
This clause governs the procedure for submitting interim and final accounts for claims arising from changes affecting Contract Price, part of the claims for change process.

This clause addresses what the Contract Price includes regarding taxes and duties and clarifies the treatment of Value Added Taxes payable by the Owner, which relates to payment mechanics under the Contract Price.

The clause requires the Contractor to submit an application for payment of the legal hypothec holdback amount following the application and payment procedures under GC 5.2 and GC 5.3, directly addressing holdback and payment mechanics.

This clause establishes the fundamental contractual duty of the Contractor to perform the Work required by the Contract Documents at the Place of the Work, which is the core work-execution obligation of the Agreement.
The clause grants the Owner authority to require inspection or testing of the Work, whether fabricated, installed, or completed, establishing an inspection right.
The provision allows review of the Design Services and inspection/testing of fabricated work to verify compliance prior to completion, reflecting a quality assurance function.

The clause addresses disputes arising under the Contract where the Consultant lacks authority and directs application of negotiation, mediation, arbitration, and rights-retention procedures, establishing a dispute-resolution process.
The clause governs procedural conditions on termination rights, allocating how default/termination risk is managed and cured between parties, tying agreements to a cure process under paragraph 8.5.1.
The clause requires the Owner to actively participate in developing and documenting the Project Objectives as part of the IPD Team, reflecting collaborative pre-construction involvement.
The Owner must provide geotechnical and environmental impact reports relevant to the Work, expressly invoking environmental considerations.

The clause establishes a requirement for how cutting and remedial work must be performed—by specialists and without damaging or endangering the Work—governing the manner of execution under the Contract Documents.

The clause allocates responsibility to the Construction Manager for damage caused to the Work, Owner's property, or adjacent property during performance of the Contract, assigning risk and liability for such damage.
The clause requires the Construction Manager to make good/correct damage at its own expense, similar to correction obligations for non-conforming conditions caused by the Construction Manager.

This clause is part of the Substantial Performance provisions under PART 5 PAYMENT, establishing the process for the Contractor to apply for a determination of Substantial Performance, which triggers payment mechanisms under the Contract.

The clause requires a comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected and clarifies that omission of an item does not relieve the Contractor of the responsibility to complete the Contract, addressing correction of deficient/incomplete Work.

The clause addresses procedures for handling a dispute that has not been resolved promptly, including the Consultant's authority to give instructions pending settlement of the dispute and preservation of claims.
The clause requires parties to act on instructions necessary for the proper performance of the Work and to prevent delays, addressing how work continues during a dispute.

This clause governs the process by which the Contractor engages Subcontractors and Suppliers to perform portions of the Work, establishing a procedural requirement for organizing the execution of the Work.

The clause allows the Owner and Construction Manager to agree to changes in Pre-construction or Construction Services without invalidating the Contract, which is a form of contractual change mechanism.
The clause governs termination of mediated negotiations by the Project Mediator when a dispute remains unresolved, directly part of the dispute resolution process under GC 7.1.

The clause establishes the Trade Contractor's general obligation to provide and pay for labour, Products, tools, equipment and services necessary to perform the Work in accordance with the Contract, a core execution duty.

The clause imposes a general obligation on the Construction Manager to comply with laws, codes, and regulations relating to performance of the Work, safety, and public health, establishing a broad duty governing how the Work is carried out.

This clause establishes that the Contract as agreed upon may only be amended through the formal mechanisms provided in the Contract Documents, reflecting a locked-in baseline agreement subject only to formal change processes.
The clause restricts amendments to the Contract to those made in accordance with the Contract Documents, which implicates the formal change order/directive provisions governing modifications.
The clause governs how the Contractor invoices for self-performed trade work awarded on a lump sum basis, addressing billing mechanics and exclusion of overhead charges.
The clause references Reimbursable Costs overhead and the Profit Pool, tying the invoicing treatment to the target cost/profit pool mechanism of the contract.

This clause imposes a duty on the Design-Builder to determine underground utility locations before commencing work, establishing a preparatory requirement governing how the Work is to be performed under the Contract Documents.

The clause establishes and adjusts the Profit Pool, a cost-related incentive mechanism tied to the Target Cost arrangement established during Validation, consistent with the GMP/Target Cost administration concept.
The clause requires the Owner to investigate and disclose toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work, directly addressing environmental hazards prior to commencement of the Work.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner for identifying and disclosing hazardous conditions, establishing an allocation of risk related to site conditions before the Contractor begins Work.

The clause establishes a formal dispute-resolution procedure requiring Notice in Writing of dispute and reply within specified time limits, and a waiver mechanism for failing to dispute a Consultant's finding.
Shop Drawings are part of the design documentation process ensuring compatibility and coordination between Construction Documents and the performance of the Work.

The clause establishes obligations on the Owner to coordinate activities of Other Contractors and Owner's own forces with the Work, addressing how work by multiple parties is executed and organized on the Project.
Clause requires that insurance coverage for Other Contractors be provided to the same requirements as GC 11.1 and coordinated with the Contractor's insurance.

The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner for compatible contract conditions, coordination, and precautions against disputes, managing risks arising from multiple contractors on the same Project.
The clause requires performance of the Work in accordance with the Project Schedule and Construction Schedule, tying execution to scheduled milestones including Ready-for-Takeover.
The clause establishes the Construction Manager's obligation to perform the Work and meet completion/end dates, a core execution duty.

The clause establishes broad Owner obligations that facilitate and enable performance of the Work, including retaining the Consultant, contracting with Trade Contractors, and providing information necessary for orderly progress of the Project.
Requires the Owner to coordinate and facilitate the Services and the Consultant's design-related services, ensuring alignment between design and construction management functions.
Obligates the Owner to pay Trade Contractors in accordance with their contracts and to designate a Payment Certifier, directly addressing payment mechanics.
Requires the Owner to immediately notify the Construction Manager upon observing any fault, defect, or non-conformity in the Work, tying into defective work identification.
This clause allocates responsibility for the Trade Contractor's failure to comply with the Contract and establishes a formal default notice and cure mechanism, managing the risk of non-performance.

The clause addresses the Trade Contractor's neglect to perform the Work properly or failure to comply with Contract requirements, requiring correction of the default within a specified period, akin to correction of non-conforming Work.

This clause establishes a baseline requirement that Products provided be new and of quality consistent with specifications, governing how the Work is performed and executed in accordance with the Contract Documents.

The clause conditions the Owner's early occupancy on regulatory approval, allocating responsibility to obtain authorization before assuming possession, which manages risk related to occupying incomplete Work.
The clause establishes the general scope and intent for performance of the Work, design, labour, and Products by the Design-Builder in accordance with the Contract Documents.
The warranty that the Work conforms to the Contract Documents establishes the standard against which non-conformance and defects are measured, underpinning correction obligations.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Design-Builder for ensuring conformity of the Work with the Contract Documents, an allocation of contractual risk.
This clause is part of the dispute resolution procedure, addressing the termination of mediated negotiations by the Project Mediator when a dispute remains unresolved.

The clause provides for adjustment of the Contract Price and Contract Time resulting from an Owner-required change of a proposed Trade Subcontractor or Supplier, which is a mechanism for adjusting price/time due to a change.

The clause requires the Contractor to execute documents vesting in the Owner the rights and benefits associated with the Contractor's obligations and commitments, effectively transferring contractual rights/title.
The clause allocates consequences and responsibilities upon termination, requiring assignment of rights as a condition of payment, reflecting risk allocation following default.
The clause allocates control/responsibility to the Contractor over selection of Subcontractors and Suppliers, allowing objection, which manages risk associated with performance by third parties.
This clause establishes the total Contract Price payable by the Owner to the Design-Builder, which is directly tied to payment provisions of the Contract.

The clause directs that disputes and matters in question between the Construction Manager and Other Contractors be resolved under Part 8 Dispute Resolution, addresses deemed consent to arbitration, and provides a mechanism for treating such disputes as between the Construction Manager and Owner absent reciprocal obligations.

The clause addresses the Owner's right to have separate contractors or its own forces perform other work on the Project, which implicates coordination and sequencing of concurrent activities at the Place of the Work.
Clause governs the PMT's approval of payment applications, including timing and amount determination, subject to Payment Legislation, which directly concerns payment certification procedures.
This clause defines the scope of the Cost of the Work for payment purposes by excluding Value Added Taxes, which relates to payment calculation mechanics under the Contract.
The clause addresses cost allocation under a Change Directive, defining what costs are covered and which are excluded due to Contractor fault, directly relating to the change mechanism.
The clause allocates responsibility for costs arising from lack of reasonable care/diligence to the Contractor, an explicit risk allocation provision.

The clause requires the Design-Builder to preserve and protect rights concerning Design Services performed by the Consultant and Other Consultants and to contract for such services, addressing coordination of design responsibility under the Contract Documents.

This clause establishes a supervisory obligation requiring the Design-Builder to provide supervision and a competent on-site representative, governing how the Work is performed and overseen at the Place of the Work.

Clause establishes how the payment application amount is determined based on proportionate value of Work performed and Products delivered as of the payment period cutoff, directly addressing payment application mechanics.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Trade Contractor for patent fees and indemnifies the Owner against claims arising from patent infringement, an explicit risk allocation mechanism.

The clause specifies entitlements to payment for Pre-construction Services fee, Fee for Construction Services, Cost of the Work, and damages upon termination, addressing payment mechanics on termination.
The clause allocates responsibility for costs and damages arising from termination by the Construction Manager, managing the financial risk consequences of contract termination.

The clause addresses non-conforming Work or Products and clarifies that payment or occupancy does not constitute acceptance of such non-conformance, preserving the Owner's right to require correction.
The clause allocates risk by ensuring that payment or use does not shift responsibility for conformity away from the Trade Contractor.
The clause establishes the Contractor's duty to provide supervision and appoint a competent representative to oversee performance of the Work at the Place of the Work, a core execution obligation.
The clause addresses the designation of a replacement Payment Certifier, the role responsible for certification of payment under the Contract, ensuring continuity of payment administration.
The clause addresses discovery of toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work and requires steps to control exposure, an environmental/hazardous materials obligation.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Design-Builder to act (stop Work, report) when hazardous substances are encountered, managing risk arising from unforeseen hazardous conditions.
The clause establishes the formal arbitration process for finally resolving disputes following unsuccessful mediation, including timing, jurisdiction, and consolidation rules.

The clause addresses that payment or use/occupancy does not constitute acceptance of non-conforming Design Services or Work, preserving the right to require correction of defective/non-conforming work.
The clause specifically references payment by the Owner and clarifies that payment does not waive non-conformance claims, tying it to payment provisions.
The clause addresses the inclusion of cash allowance work value in progress payments, directly relating to payment application mechanics.

This clause establishes a waiver and release of claims after a defined period, allocating and limiting liability risk between the Owner and Construction Manager subject to applicable limitation statutes.

The clause establishes that conflicts or disagreements between the parties shall be settled through negotiation, mediation, and arbitration procedures under GC 7.1, constituting a formal dispute-resolution mechanism.
Clause describes the process for proposing a change in the Work and requiring the Contractor to present adjustment methods for Fee, price, and Contract Time, which is the core Change Order mechanism.
The clause explicitly requires adjustment amounts/methods for the GMP or Target Contract Price as part of the change process.
Establishing the warranty period defines the timeframe during which defective or non-conforming Work must be corrected under the Contract's warranty provisions.
The clause governs the formalization of agreed adjustments to Contract Price and Contract Time through a Change Order, part of the change management mechanism under a Change Directive process.

The clause defines the amount applied for in progress payment applications, based on cost of Work performed, Products delivered, and Contractor's Fee earned, directly governing payment application mechanics.
References Products delivered to the Place of the Work or other locations designated by the Owner, tying payment to delivery of Products.
This clause is part of GC 6.6 governing claims for a change in Contract Price, requiring the claiming party to mitigate loss and keep records supporting the claim.

The clause governs how trade work may be performed under the Contract, specifically allowing the Contractor to self-perform certain trade work subject to PMT agreement, establishing a scope allocation mechanism for execution of the Work.
This clause establishes a general obligation on the Construction Manager to perform and fulfill everything required by the Contract Documents, a broad Work execution duty.
The clause governs the release and payment timing of holdback amounts to the Trade Contractor in accordance with lien and payment legislation.
This clause establishes the claim procedure for adjusting the Contract Price, requiring Notice in Writing of intent to claim, which is part of the change/claims mechanism under the Contract.
The clause allocates responsibility for identifying, reporting, and managing the risk of mould at the Place of the Work, including retaining an independent expert when parties disagree.
Requires the Contractor to take reasonable steps, including stopping the Work, to prevent harm from mould, directly affecting how the Work is performed.

The clause defines disputes and mandates that unresolved differences be settled in accordance with the dispute resolution procedures set out in Part 8 of the General Conditions, directly establishing the dispute resolution process trigger.
The clause addresses the timing and payment of the holdback amount and permits retention of sums for legal hypothecs or third-party claims, directly governing payment mechanics under the Contract.

The clause defines the scope of the Consultant's review of Shop Drawings as limited to conformity with the design concept and general arrangement, addressing design consistency and coordination between Shop Drawings and Contract Documents.
The clause addresses allocation of insurance deductible amounts under the required policies, directly relating to insurance coverage administration.

The clause directs that where concealed/unknown conditions differ materially and affect Fee, GMP, Target Contract Price, or Contract Time, a change is implemented through Change Order or Change Directive processes, directly invoking the change mechanism.
The clause specifically identifies adjustments to GMP and Target Contract Price resulting from the finding on concealed conditions, tying the change to these cost mechanisms.
The clause addresses the Owner's investigation of the impact on Design Services or Work resulting from discoveries, which typically leads to adjustments in the Work, Contract Price, or Contract Time.
The clause requires a joint schedule showing timing for authorization of ordering, directly addressing scheduling and timing to avoid delaying progress of the Work.

The schedule is specifically intended to ensure timely authorization for ordering items under cash allowances so that procurement does not delay the progress of the Work, tying schedule impacts to procurement/ordering timing.
The Contractor and Consultant are required to jointly prepare the schedule, reflecting collaborative planning between the parties.
The Consultant reviews the Project to verify whether it has attained Ready-for-Takeover, which is an inspection/verification process to confirm compliance with completion criteria.
The clause establishes responsibility for the Consultant to certify or reject completion status, allocating responsibility for determining conformity of the Work.

The clause establishes the process and consequences for the Contractor's failure to comply with Contract requirements, allocating responsibility for default and remedy, which is part of risk allocation and management under the Contract.

The clause addresses the Contractor's neglect to perform the Work properly, i.e., non-conforming performance, and requires correction of the default within a specified time, which aligns with the correction of defective/non-conforming Work.
The clause requires notification of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, directly relating to identification of non-conforming Work for correction.

The clause establishes that the Contractor remains responsible for executing the design or specified method of construction for Temporary Work in the same manner as for the Work, defining a duty regarding how the Work is performed.

The clause allocates responsibility between design (not the Contractor's responsibility) and execution (the Contractor's responsibility) for Temporary Work designs or specified methods of construction, an explicit risk allocation.
The clause addresses how designs for Temporary Work or specified construction methods are treated as part of the design of the Work, clarifying design responsibility boundaries.
